findings.finding: Step 4 cannot meet the stated success criterion that a no-match regex is not counted as an update. In the config-driven loop, aid-release.sh unconditionally appends every configured FULL_PATH to /tmp/aid-release-updated-$$ after the regex branch, even when sed changed no bytes. The path is then appended to UPDATED[], which drives the printed total, rollback set, and prepare-plan staging set. Step 4 only suppresses the per-row Updated message and explicitly leaves counting to Step 3, while Step 3 is scoped to the fallback bookkeeping and no dependency connects the two steps.
findings.recommendation: Make the regex branch return an explicit changed/already-current/miss result and append to the temporary UPDATED list only for changed files. Pin the no-match case against the per-row output, Updated total, UPDATED/staging set, and rollback set; alternatively fold this shared bookkeeping into Step 3 and declare the dependency.

findings.finding: The runner refusal has an undeclared external prerequisite: the repaired self-host config must merge before the refusal, and every live worktree must refresh before its next run. The plan nevertheless declares Depends on: none and Blocks: none. aid-worktree-report.sh only reports worktrees; it neither refreshes them nor proves that every profile inclusion has a command. This is material because the existing P080 worktree has its own tracked execution.yaml with the command-less plan_diff gate, so shipping the refusal first breaks its gate run.
findings.recommendation: Represent the migration as an explicit prerequisite/order with a finite, machine-verifiable completion condition, or make the refusal compatibility-aware until a config generation/version proves migration. State the required commits/checkouts and add a test or gate that exercises the affected-worktree condition before enabling the refusal.

findings.finding: The criterion requiring the live baseline's percentiles to be numerically identical before and after is not self-contained or reproducible. The baseline is the mutable, CWD-relative .aid-o/metrics/gate-runtime-baselines.yaml (or AID_GATE_BASELINE_FILE override), not a tracked fixture or sealed input, and ordinary gate execution writes it. The proposed test path has no specified baseline snapshot or expected percentile values, so it cannot verify this AC deterministically.
findings.recommendation: Replace the live-baseline claim with a tracked legacy fixture passed through AID_GATE_BASELINE_FILE and assert explicit percentile outputs, or provide a sealed baseline fixture and exact before/after comparison command.
